description: Create a post. FASTEST for media posts: pass mediaUrls (public https URLs — Publora downloads them server-side) together with scheduledTime to create AND schedule in one call; platforms like Instagram, TikTok, YouTube require media before scheduling. For a ChatGPT file, omit scheduledTime to create a draft, then use attach_media. Manual alternative for local files: omit scheduledTime to create a draft, upload media with get_upload_url + HTTP PUT + complete_media (once per file), then call update_post with status 'scheduled'.

content.description: Post text content. With Threads threading enabled, long content auto-splits into replies; use a standalone --- line between paragraphs for explicit breaks. Media are attached only to the first part.

platforms.description: Optional platform TYPES to restrict the comment to, e.g. ['linkedin', 'threads'] — NOT connection keys. Omit to comment on every supported target.

text.description: Comment text, posted as-is. Measured the way each platform counts: X 280 (25000 on Premium; URLs count 23), LinkedIn 1250, Threads 500, Bluesky 300 graphemes / 3000 bytes, Mastodon 500 (links count 23).

firstComment.description: Optional first comment: one text comment Publora posts under your own post right after it publishes (hashtags, 'link in the comments'). Supported now: linkedin (profiles and Pages), twitter, threads, bluesky, mastodon — other targets are skipped with a warning. Best effort: Publora never repeats an ambiguous attempt; read each post's firstCommentResult via get_post. Cannot be added after publishing.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional retry key. Reusing it with the identical request replays the original response without creating another post.

mediaUrls.description: Optional array (max 10) of public https URLs of images/videos to attach. Downloaded and validated server-side (jpeg, png, gif, webp, tiff, avif, mp4, mov, webm; images ≤25MB, videos ≤150MB). Must be DIRECT file URLs — share-page links (Google Drive, Dropbox pages) will fail.

platformSettings.description: Per-platform publishing options, keyed by platform. Example: { instagram: { coverUrl: 'https://.../cover.jpg' }, youtube: { title: 'My video', madeForKids: false }, tiktok: { viewerSetting: 'SELF_ONLY' }, linkedin: { repostEnabled: true, repostParentUrn: 'urn:li:share:123', repostVisibility: 'PUBLIC' }, twitter: { replyTo: 'https://x.com/user/status/123' } }. Unknown platforms or fields are rejected.

coverUrl.description: Public https URL of a JPEG Reels cover image

repostParentUrn.description: Canonical LinkedIn post URN to repost; activity URNs are not supported

quoteTweet.description: Quote this tweet: full tweet URL or bare numeric tweet ID (applied to the first tweet of a thread). May be combined with replyTo and with media. Empty string clears. Subject to the same X restriction as replyTo: the target author must have mentioned this account in that post or quoted one of its posts, unless this account wrote the target itself.

replyTo.description: Publish the X post as a reply to this tweet: full tweet URL (x.com/twitter.com .../status/<id>) or bare numeric tweet ID. A thread chains under the target. Empty string clears. IMPORTANT: X only accepts a programmatic reply when the target post's author mentioned this account IN THAT POST, quoted one of its posts, or when this account wrote it — replying to an unrelated third-party tweet fails at publish time. Use it for answering mentions, not for cold outreach.

platforms.description: Array of platform identifiers in the exact format returned by list_connections. Each value must be the 'platformId' field copied verbatim from a connection object, e.g. ['twitter-1985855679454986200', 'linkedin-abc123']. IMPORTANT: Do NOT invent or guess IDs — always call list_connections first and use the exact platformId values. Exception: 'publora-playground' is a connection-test target that requires no real connection — the post is acknowledged and discarded, nothing is published; when used it must be the ONLY entry.

scheduledTime.description: Optional ISO 8601 datetime for publishing, e.g. '2025-03-01T12:00:00Z'. Omit to create a draft. Scheduling a media-requiring platform without media fails validation — pass mediaUrls in the same call to avoid that.
